clue.text: Ned has worked in the country and gives help

indicators.note: in tells us the shuffled letters sit inside the word for the country

parts.note: land is a country or nation

indicators.note: worked as in worked over or kneaded, so the letters of Ned and has are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ned has laboured on the farm and lends assistance to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' is the anagram signal rather than labour on a farm, and 'in' places the result inside the country, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend a hand is the everyday idiom for assisting someone, which is what giving help means.

clue.text: Boy without independence may be put down

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for boy wraps around the letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy
I is the standard abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: A boy deprived of his freedom might be crushed or humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: LAD goes around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past participle of lay, so something laid has been set or placed on a surface.

clue.text: Time of life coming up for little sleeps

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a span is a lifetime, the length of a life

explanation.surface: A point in life arrives for taking short rests, perhaps old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns SPAN, the span of a life, into NAPS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Naps are short spells of rest during the day, brief dozes rather than a full night's slumber.

clue.text: Place in which priest's found fairy

indicators.note: in which ... found says the priest's abbreviation is set within the word for place

parts.note: a site is a place or location
PR is a recognised abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: A location where a clergyman comes upon a fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' marks the container; the priest is reduced to his standard two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or pixie, a small supernatural creature of folklore.

clue.text: Flowers that every hotel en-suite should have!

definitions.text: Flowers that every hotel en-suite should have!

parts.words: Flowers that every hotel en-suite should have!
parts.note: Flowers is read as things that flow rather than blooms: the two supplies running from the taps of any hotel bathroom

explanation.surface: A suggestion that every hotel bathroom ought to have a vase of blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' wants to be blossoms; it is things that flow, as liquid out of a tap.
explanation.definitionFit: Every properly equipped bathroom has both heated and unheated supplies running from its taps, the flowing things meant here.

clue.text: Stories of knight and various loves

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of loves are mixed into a different order

explanation.surface: Tales of a chivalrous knight and his many romances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' signals the anagram; in chess notation the knight is N, because K is already taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Novels are long works of prose fiction, books that tell tales.

clue.text: Restrain black dog to start with

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: to start with tells us to use only the opening letter of black

explanation.surface: An instruction to hold back a dark-coated dog from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb something is to check or hold it in, as a rider reins in a horse.

clue.text: I am a dunce upsetting college — not scholarly

indicators.note: upsetting in the sense of overturning, so the letters of I am a dunce are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A self-confessed dunce admits to disrupting a college, plainly no intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges IAMADUNCE into UNACADEMI; C for college finishes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unacademic lacks bookish learning or interest in formal study.

clue.text: Growing desire to get on admitted by crooner

indicators.note: admitted by means let inside, so the crooner's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the archetypal crooner
an urge is a desire
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer lets in a mounting wish to make progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted by' marks the container; the crooner is Bing Crosby, the American singer famous for 'White Christmas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgeoning means flourishing or expanding quickly, as buds swell in spring.

clue.text: Sort of mood not to be ignored

definitions.meaning: in grammar, the mood of a verb used for commands
essential, vitally important, so that it must be attended to

explanation.surface: A frame of mind that demands attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names the command form of a verb this way, and the same word means urgent or essential.

clue.text: Pretty good trade show

definitions.meaning: moderately good, reasonable, as in a reasonable chance
an exhibition where goods are displayed and sold

explanation.surface: A trade exhibition that is reasonably decent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means reasonable or middling in quality, and also an exhibition where traders gather to sell.

clue.text: Carol goes round van, scurrying

indicators.note: goes round says the word for carol wraps itself around the vehicle

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a camper is a camper van, a vehicle for living in on holiday

explanation.surface: A woman named Carol hurries about the van in a fluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name, but it is the verb, and 'goes round' puts it around the holiday vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampering is running with quick light steps, like a mouse dashing about.

clue.text: It's misguided, making pope saint, I fancy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: fancy as a verb, imagining the letters of pope saint I in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it a mistake to canonise a pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' signals an anagram of POPE, SAINT and I, while the clue's I also joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inapposite is out of place or wrongly applied, an ill-judged remark or choice.

clue.text: Sensing a thrill by the fireside

parts.note: at means by or next to, as in at the door
an ingle is a fireplace or hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: Feeling a shiver of excitement while sitting near the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: INGLE is an old word for a fireplace, best known from 'inglenook'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be atingle is to be tingling, quivering with excitement or anticipation.

clue.text: Insects? Old man being upset goes under cover

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word for father reads upwards

parts.note: the old man is slang for father, PA
to hide is to go under cover

explanation.surface: A father upset by bugs scurries off to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' turns PA into AP. The question mark admits that aphides is a rare plural of aphis.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphides is a plural of aphis, the greenfly or blackfly that sucks plant sap.

clue.text: English revolutionary taking half of capital with troop formation

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's favourite revolutionary

indicators.note: half of means only the first three of the capital's six letters are kept

parts.note: London is the capital city of the UK

explanation.surface: An English rebel seizes part of the capital along with a column of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' drops DON from LONDON, leaving LON.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a stepped arrangement of troops, ships or aircraft, each unit offset from the one ahead.

clue.text: Appetising food from tin given to zoo animal?

parts.note: a can is a tin
an ape is an animal found in a zoo

explanation.surface: Feeding a zoo creature something tasty out of a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the ape is only one example of a zoo animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury snack served before a meal or with drinks.

clue.text: Quarrel with energy, being in a tight corner

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or quarrel
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A fierce argument breaks out among people trapped in a difficult situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament, a fix someone has got themselves into.

clue.text: Offering pleasure in a fiendish way — then a simple hope is shattered

definitions.text: Offering pleasure in a fiendish way

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters of then a simple hope are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A devil tempts with delights, and then an innocent's wish is dashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is shattered' rearranges THEN A SIMPLE HOPE. Mephistopheles is the devil of the Faust legend, who offers Faust earthly pleasures in exchange for his soul.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil of the Faust story tempted with delights; the adjective describes such diabolical temptation.

clue.text: Runs to marriage finally?

parts.note: describes a couple running off in secret who end up wed at the end of their flight

explanation.surface: Someone who eventually ends up at the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' suggests running, or a cricket score; here a couple slip away secretly to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who run away together secretly do so to get married without consent.

clue.text: Quickly purchase pans!

parts.note: the first word put up, read upwards in this down light, gives the clue word pans

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay, SNAP with UP turning it in a down entry, gives the clue's 'pans'.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap something up is to buy it eagerly before anyone else can.

clue.text: External preparation — simple person swallows it wrongly

indicators.note: swallows means takes inside, so the fool's word holds the jumbled letters

parts.note: a loon is a fool, a simpleton

indicators.note: wrongly suggests the two letters of it are placed in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A gullible fellow drinks an ointment by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' swaps the two letters of 'it', and 'swallows' sets them inside the word for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is a liquid applied to the skin, a medicine for outward use only.

clue.text: Sail after due time and finally make Southampton

parts.note: late means after the expected or proper time

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: A yacht, behind schedule, eventually reaches the port of Southampton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from 'make' and N from 'Southampton'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lateen is a triangular sail on a long sloping yard, used on Mediterranean boats.

clue.text: A fellow who gets left out in the cold

definitions.text: A fellow who gets left out in the cold

parts.words: A fellow who gets left out in the cold
parts.note: left out in the cold usually means ignored; here it is literal, a figure built and left standing in the winter garden

explanation.surface: A man who is excluded and ignored by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'left out in the cold' suggests someone shunned; taken literally, it is a figure made of frozen flakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure built from packed winter flakes stands outdoors in freezing weather, a 'man' left out literally.

clue.text: Girl from Dublin perhaps taking hour off

indicators.note: taking ... off means removing the letter for hour from the nationality

parts.note: someone from Dublin is Irish; perhaps marks Dublin as one example

explanation.surface: A young woman from the Irish capital, it seems, clocks off early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes H for hour from IRISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a woman's given name, as in the novelist Iris Murdoch.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink for short-story writer

definitions.meaning: the Japanese rice wine, a variant spelling of sake
the pen name of H. H. Munro, Edwardian author of witty short stories

explanation.surface: A booze-loving author of short fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Saki was the pen name of H. H. Munro (1870-1916).
explanation.definitionFit: The spelling names both the Japanese rice wine and the pen name of the Edwardian author H. H. Munro.

clue.text: It goes through city (Newcastle)

indicators.note: the answer runs through the clue words, spanning the end of one and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Something flows through the middle of Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes through' finds the answer across 'ciTY NEwcastle'; the whole clue also describes the river that flows through Newcastle, in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The river of north-east England flows through Newcastle on its way to the North Sea.

clue.text: A hearty cop out to get someone peddling drugs once

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrong or disordered, so the letters of A hearty cop are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheerful policeman goes undercover to arrest a drug dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges A HEARTY COP. 'peddling drugs' suggests a dealer, but an apothecary was an old-fashioned chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecary was the old name for a pharmacist, who prepared and sold medicines.

clue.text: Joy when good shelter is found

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Happiness comes when good protection is located.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great delight or merriment.

clue.text: Someone not yet an expert could make Peter panic

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters of Peter panic can be formed into something new

explanation.surface: A novice might cause someone called Peter to lose his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges PETER PANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is a learner bound to a skilled worker to master a trade.
